interest: Covers 1930s US intelligence in Hawaii and a 1936 memo on Lt.-Col. Aizawa's murder trial as radical 'Showa Restoration' politics.
overview: Combines a 1932-35 docket on Japanese intelligence activity in Hawaii with a March 1936 Far Eastern Affairs memo on Lt.-Col. Saburo Aizawa's court-martial for murdering Maj.-Gen. Tetsuzan Nagata, read as a radical 'Showa Restoration' political trial before the February 26 Incident.

people.name: Kilsoo Haan
people.role: Representative of the Sino-Korean People's League

people.name: Valentine Stuart McClatchy
people.role: Executive Secretary of the California Joint Immigration Committee

subfiles.about: A State Department docket sheet listing interdepartmental reports from 1932 to 1935 on Japanese intelligence gathering, naval surveillance, and language school propaganda in Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Lists seven War/Navy Department reports (1932-35) on Japanese tanker surveillance, language-school loyalty efforts, and petitions from Kilsoo Haan and McClatchy.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Japanese Military Activities in Hawaii

subfiles.about: A State Department Far Eastern Affairs memorandum analyzing Tokyo Embassy Despatch No. 1707 on the court-martial of Lieutenant-Colonel Aizawa and its connection to radical military unrest.
subfiles.summary: Division of Far Eastern Affairs memo on Lt.-Col. Saburo Aizawa's court-martial for the August 1935 murder of Maj.-Gen. Tetsuzan Nagata, calling it a propaganda trial reflecting army radicals' drive for a 'Showa Restoration', postponed after the February 26 Incident.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on the Trial of Lieutenant-Colonel Aizawa for the Murder of Major-General Nagata
